summary.name: LiteLLM
summary.one_liner: LiteLLM is an open-source AI gateway and LLM proxy that exposes 140+ model providers behind one OpenAI-compatible API, with spend tracking, budgets, and routing.
keywords: access one api for many llms
use_cases: Give a company-wide team access to many LLM providers through one key
Track and cap AI API spend per team or project
Route simple prompts to cheaper models and hard prompts to stronger ones
Self-host an LLM proxy in Kubernetes or an air-gapped environment
Attribute AI usage costs for internal chargeback
Put MCP servers and agents behind the same gateway as LLMs
summary.what_it_does: LiteLLM provides a single OpenAI-compatible API that reaches more than 140 providers and 1,800+ models, so applications can swap models without code changes. It tracks usage and spend per key, user, team, and model, and can enforce hard budgets and rate limits that stop requests at the cap. Routing features include load balancing across providers, regions, and keys, lowest-cost routing, and Auto Routing between cheaper and stronger models. The gateway can be self-hosted via Docker, Helm, or Terraform on your own Postgres and Redis, including fully air-gapped setups. The page also describes a Rust-based gateway with a claimed 0.66 ms p99 overhead, based on the vendor's own benchmark.
notable: MIT-licensed open-source gateway with an enterprise tier adding SSO, RBAC, audit logs and support
Hard per-key, team, and model budgets with daily or monthly resets that stop requests at the cap
Claimed sub-millisecond overhead (0.66 ms p99) for the Rust AI Gateway, from the vendor's own benchmark
Also routes agents and MCP servers through the same gateway
caveats: Enterprise features such as SSO, RBAC, audit logs and SLAs are paid add-ons on top of the open-source core
Performance numbers and download counts are vendor-reported; pulls and downloads are not installs or users
